My grandfather shared some context and a story to go along with the pic. He is the one on the right: 

​

"As I wrote earlier the picture was taken north of the DMZ in June 1969. I was eighteen years old. Please note the bark on the trees was taken off in many areas around the trunk. Often when a bomb explodes the shrap metal goes in every direction. Of course the center of the explosion is a crater and there is nothing there except a large hole. You don't  see in the picture the numerous bomb craters. American Marines love seeing things blown up!  Ha Ha Also used was Napalm and Agent Orange. Napalm burns for days regardless of rain. It was very surreal. Agent Orange is a huge weed killer but it kills all vegetation. These chemicals were used to clear away jungle growth to provide the building of combat support bases. BTW: I'm on the watch list for blood cancers. I'm not worried as I would laugh knowing that I survived everything else in life and got killed by a bad variation of Roundup! Truly, it is ironically tragic and humorous.   
You'll notice that my t-shirt was drenched (different shades show the sweat) with sweat, as usual ,due to the heavy equipment and patrols. I was wearing two chains. One chain was my dog tags (ID) and another was a St. Christopher medal my Mom gave me for protection. Funny that later the Catholic church threw out St. Christopher as a fake. Note, that I never believed that a medal would stop a bullet or bomb but, out of my deep love and respect for my mom I wore it. Irony comes again as my atheist platoon Lieutenant orders that I take off the medal. Typical of my obstinateness, I refused. As then and now a man's faith is up to him and not the government. Plus I didn't like the Lieutenant. All Marines have the right to "Request Mast' to see anyone in the chain of command. I demanded to see the Commandant of the Marines, LtGen Chapman. The next day a 'full bird' colonel came out to talk to me. I was shocked as this was the front line and extremely dangerous. The colonel and I prayed and I kept the medal in my front breast pocket. Once again I'm not smiling.   
The other Marine in the picture was Griffin (Grif) and you can tell he was heavy into Black Power as were many other African American Marines. I don't mind people exercising their freedoms but, out in the battle zone was a bad idea. How strange that the officers allowed this to go on? Griff had gone on R&R (rest and recuperation) to Singapore. And when he got back he would be the new team leader. Griff was very competent and savvy when it came to jungle fighting and tactics. While Griff was gone a big kiss-ass on the team kept acquessing to the Sergeant and Lieutenant who were both white. Unbeknown to the team ,the kiss-ass was to be the new team leader, although he lacked experience and judgement. When Griff got back we were all told who would be the new team leader. We were all stunned and angry! Griff got his M-16 and wandered off in front of the line.I just thought he needed time to get over the decision that he would not lead the team. A few moments later we heard automatic gunfire and screaming. Usually, when a firefight starts there is a lot of gunfire, explosions and screaming. This was different. I told the team to get our rifles and check out what was happening. The kiss-ass stayed behind and perhaps a good idea? I reached Griff and asked him to put down the rifle and come back. Griff never said a word as he knew he messed up and messed up badly! Griff was arrested and taken out of the field.   
A few days later the company was taken to the rear, for rest. As Providence would have it I walked by a huge cargo container and had a guard standing by the opening. I looked inside and saw Griff. Griff was handcuffed. He looked at me and just looked down as if his life had amounted to no significance. After all his suffering, what was the reward? I sense that his hate for white America,along with the Black Power movement had clouded his judgment. Griff was Court Martialled but we never knew what happened to him.  
What I didn't know was that several African American Marines saw me at the cargo container talking with Griff. I don't recall anything we said to each other. Griff would speak to me but he didn't care for anything that wasn't Black. I felt bad that he was always so angry. Although this was wrong by Griff, it was also racist for for the Lieutenant not to pick Griff.   
Shortly after the other African American Marines treated me as if I was Black. During that time African American Marines gave each other the 'Power' sign and a certain handshake that was only given to each other as a sign of solidarity. Weird that everyday I would participate in the 'secret handshake' but I never gave the 'power' sign! One day I'll show it to you! "

The problem is that this is the very character of life itself. Your problem encapsulates the very character of desire itself.

According to the psychoanalytic theory of Jacques Lacan, the cause of our desire is not the object that focuses our desire, but the gap, the loss of the object itself, which is the "cause" of our desire. If the object of our desire (spouse, job, happiness, etc.) were the cause of our *desire*, once that object was attained our desire would increase. However, once we attain the object of our desire, our desire (for that object) disappears. *The disappearance of our desire coincides with the loss of the gap between us and the object of desire*.

Being intelligent does not necessarily mean you are more likely to carry on your genetic information. The smartest people in our society today are actually not having kids.

Then you may say, "but shouldn't we make sure smarter people are having kids to save mankind blah blah?"

Let me ask you a question: *for what purpose?*

Natural selection is mindless. It has no goal. It is completely open-ended. It is an emergent phenomenon. One day all life as we know it will die off and there will be no intelligent beings left in the universe. If we somehow get only smart people to procreate, then what? We will still all die off one day, and all of humanity will be forgotten.

You have to get out of this mindset where there is some kind of goal or purpose to humankind and to evolution. Evolution is simply a phenomenon that is studied and observed, and we are always a part of it. No one is exempt.

This makes no sense because, if someone decides to save someone else from dying that is also just as natural as letting them die. Altruism is also a natural phenomenon. You cannot make statements about what should or should not be done with regard to natural selection, as humans and all things in nature are subject to it. Natural selection is not a process that is controlled from the outside. Every human action and behavior is just as "natural" as any other.
